errorCodes.meaning: `refresh` was asked and the VTA could not read its account from the host. The details say why; the response the VTA would otherwise give is unchanged, and a request without `refresh` still answers from what it recorded.

AccountReferral.description: A Referral as the service recorded it on an account, with whether anything other than the registrant's own word supports it.

verified.description: `true` when the admission evidence supports it: a voucher whose issuer is `via`, or an invite whose administrator set the referral when issuing it. `false`: the registrant's own claim, recorded for attribution only.

AccountReferral.title: AccountReferral

AccountState.description: Where an account stands in the inactivity lifecycle. `active`: its DIDs are served. `warned`: its DIDs are served, `disableAt` is near, and the service has sent at least one expiry notice. `disabled`: its DIDs are not served; the holder may still renew until `purgeAt`. A purged account no longer exists and is reported as not found.
AccountState.title: AccountState

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

HostingAccount.description: One account on a DID hosting service: who holds it, how it was admitted, and where it stands in the service's inactivity lifecycle.

admission.description: How the account was admitted: `invite`, an operator-issued invite; `voucher`, a voucher from a trust community the domain trusts. Absent for an account an administrator created directly.

disableAt.description: When the account's DIDs will be disabled if nothing keeps the account alive before then. Present for an `active` or `warned` account that is subject to expiry; absent for an account that is not (one an administrator exempted, for example) and for a `disabled` one.

domain.description: The hosting domain the account was admitted on. A self-registered account may hold DIDs on this domain only.

exempt.description: `true` when an administrator has exempted the account from its domain's terms (did-management/account/exempt): no path prefixes, agent names allowed, no inactivity lifecycle. Absent or `false`: the terms apply. Only on a self-registered account.

lastActiveAt.description: The last time the holder sent a task the service accepted, renewals included. A service MAY record this coarsely (for example at most once a day); it is a liveness signal, not an audit trail. Absent when the service has recorded none since registration.

lastResolvedAt.description: The last time any of the account's DIDs was resolved from the service, as far as the service knows. Absent when the service does not count resolutions toward liveness or has recorded none.

maxDidCount.description: The most DIDs the account may hold. Absent when the service does not state one.

maxTotalSizeBytes.description: The most bytes of DID content the account may hold in total. Absent when the service does not state one.

purgeAt.description: When a `disabled` account, its DIDs and its access are deleted. Present exactly when `state` is `disabled`.

role.description: The role the hosting service holds the account under, in the service's own role vocabulary (opaque here, as in the acl/* family) — for a self-registered account, its ordinary DID-owner role. What sets a self-registered account apart is not its role but its terms: its domain's path prefixes, quotas and inactivity lifecycle, and no agent names.

subject.description: The DID that holds the account, exactly as it authenticated when it registered. A `did:scid` subject is recorded without its `src` query parameter, which locates the log and is not part of the identity.

HostingAccount.title: HostingAccount

account.description: The account as the host last reported it, verbatim. Absent until the VTA has heard from the host since registering.

checkedAt.description: When `account` was last read from the host, by a renewal, a status read or an expiry notice.

domain.description: The domain the account is on, as the host names it (a host, with a port when one is not the default).

lastError.description: Why the VTA's last attempt to reach the host failed, as the operator should read it. Absent once a later attempt succeeds.

lastNotice.description: The latest did-management/account/expiry-notice the host sent and the VTA accepted.

receivedAt.description: When the VTA accepted the notice.

stage.description: The notice's stage, as did-management/account/expiry-notice names it: the account is about to be disabled, has been, or is about to be purged.

registeredAt.description: When the host opened the account.

renewedAt.description: When the host last accepted a renewal (did-management/account/renew).

serverDid.description: The DID hosting service's DID — the only party whose expiry notices the VTA accepts for this account.

Response.description: Whether the VTA holds a self-registered hosting account, and if it does, what it knows about it. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

registered.description: Whether this VTA holds a self-registered hosting account. false: it never self-registered (its DID is hosted some other way, or by the VTA itself), and `hosting` is absent.

schema.description: A VTA's principal asks for the state of the account the VTA holds on the DID hosting service it self-registered with. The request names no account: a VTA holds at most one self-registered hosting account. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

refresh.description: Ask the host before answering: the VTA reads its account with did-management/account/status (which counts as no activity) and answers with what the host said. Absent or false: the VTA answers from what it last recorded, without contacting the host.

schema.title: VTA Hosting Account — Get — payload
